newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds hold steady in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds hold steady in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Irish government bonds remained steady in sluggish afternoon trade on Tuesday as the market waited for something to stimulate trading, dealers said.

"Volume has been very low for most of the day. The 10-year bond has seen the most of the action and rose a little. Things are still a little muted after Monday's UK bank holiday and around this time many investors are on holiday," one dealer said.
By 1515 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was down five pence at 103.80 to yield 6.79 percent. The eight percent bond due 2006 rose seven pence to 102.82 to yield 7.45 percent.
Dealers said they were focusing on Wednesday's sale of 2.5 billion stg of 10-year UK gilts, which would provide a litmus-test for markets in Dublin and London.
In the UK September gilt futures ended 11/32 lower after a thin trading session in which the market took its cue from weak internation bond markets.
Irish dealers said the main domestic focus would be Friday's Irish retail sales figures for June.
